The Client: 

ZED Real Estate is an industry-disrupting, high-performance luxury property group and is known as one of the most digitally progressive real estate advisory firms in Australia. Due to their expanding international footprint of advisors and corporate offices spanning Melbourne, Queensland, and Dubai, their infrastructure requires enterprise-grade engineering and now seek an experienced Computer?Network and System Engineer to join the team in Hampton East, Victoria. 

?? 

The Role: 

This is a full time role with an annual salary set at $150,000 plus superannuation, and will be based in Hampton East, Victoria. 

? 

The Responsibilities: 

Design, deploy, and manage secure, high-availability Local Area Networks (LAN), Wide Area Networks (WAN), and wireless environments across all corporate offices, including Hampton East (VIC), Mermaid Beach (QLD), and Dubai. 

Implement advanced networking technologies and configure routers, firewalls, and network switches to prioritise high-bandwidth traffic, ensuring seamless VoIP communication.  

Create, update, and maintain detailed technical documentation, including network inventories, configuration change logs, maintenance procedures, and fault resolution records. 

Design and deploy network configurations, incorporating high-availability routing protocols, Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs), Quality of Service (QoS) rules, and secure site-to-site VPN tunnels. 

Implement SoftwareDefined Networking (SDN) and develop programmatic, APIdriven workflows across network hardware using automation tools such as PowerShell, Bash, Python, and RESTful integrations to improve operational efficiency and system reliability. 

Monitor and analyse network traffic, capacity, and utilisation metrics, and evaluate endtoend network infrastructure performance across all corporate office locations. 

Evaluate and propose technical enhancements to network operations, interconnected server infrastructure, internal hardware, distributed PropTech applications, and hybrid operational environments. 

Optimise 4K media-rendering architectures and secure localised Network attached Storage (NAS) configurations, improving internal high-volume data-pipeline workflows for the marketing division. 

Oversee network and system configurations to ensure smooth data flows between real estate-specific APIs, external listing syndications (e.g., Realestate.com.au, Domain), and internal master CRMs. 

Provision, test, and deploy complex server networks, cloud systems (Microsoft 365, Azure Active Directory / Entra ID), and endpoint systems using modern Mobile Device Management (MDM) software. 

Formulate comprehensive testing strategies to validate network throughput, failover systems, and server redundancy, ensuring the agency maintains its strict zero-downtime metric during business hours. 

Provide expert troubleshooting and fault-finding services to isolate, diagnose, and resolve intricate network bugs, hardware failures, system anomalies, or cross-platform software conflicts. 

Troubleshoot complex issues across hardware, networks, software, database applications, servers, and workstations, coordinating with internal teams and vendors, and maintaining high service standards. 

Actively contribute to ZED Real Estate’s Information Security Management System (ISMS) by supporting the implementation and upkeep of its policies, procedures and controls, ensuring the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information in alignment with ISO/IEC?27001. 

Design and execute network security baselines, including Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW), Zero-Trust conditional access rules, Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), and advanced endpoint detection systems. 

Architect and manage Identity and Access Management (IAM) lifecycle workflows to enforce continuous security baselines across automated user onboarding and offboarding frameworks. 

Create, test, and preserve robust data backup structures, comprehensive disaster recovery workflows, and Business Continuity Plans (BCP) to secure sensitive real estate escrow accounts and high-net-worth data. 

 

The Requirements: 

A Bachelor’s degree or higher qualification in Network Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a closely related ICT Major. 

At least 5 years of relevant professional experience as a Network Engineer, Systems Engineer, or ICT Systems Administrator in a corporate setting 

Professional infrastructure certifications are highly regarded (e.g., Cisco CCNA/CCNP, Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator, CompTIA Security+). 

At least 5 years demonstrated experience of core networking models and protocols (TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, BGP, VPN, switching, routing). 

At least 5 years experience managing corporate directory platforms and infrastructure identities (Microsoft cloud technologies, including Microsoft 365, Entra and Intune). 

Must have over 5 years’ experience to implement, administer, and troubleshoot network infrastructure devices, including wireless access points, firewall, routers, switches, controllers 

Must know how to setup virtual configurations in VMWare vSphere and Hyper-V 

At least 5 years of experience with server virtualisation, cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), and hybrid integration projects. 

Strong analytical skills and sound administration skills 

Quick to grasp new ideas and concepts 

Ability to work to tight deadlines and under immense pressure at times

result.description:
Sunup Farm at Spring Creek, Queensland, is a certified organic horticultural grower that cultivates and supplies fresh produce to markets across the region. The business runs the full growing cycle in house, from crop production and irrigation through to harvesting, packing and dispatch, and holds organic certification across a broad range of vegetable and fruit lines. With a firm commitment to product quality, workplace safety, sustainable growing practices and employment within the regional community, Sunup Farm is looking for an experienced Quality Assurance Manager to join the team. As Sunup Farm continues to grow and to uphold the standards behind its certifications, we are bringing quality assurance and food safety under dedicated leadership. Reporting to management, the Quality Assurance Manager will take ownership of the systems, standards and everyday checks that keep our produce safe, consistent and compliant, from the paddock through to the packing shed and on to our customers.

In this role you will:
•	Build and maintain the farm's quality assurance and food safety management systems, so every line of produce consistently meets the standards our customers and certifiers expect.
•	Identify the food safety standards, organic certification requirements and regulatory codes that apply to our operation, and turn them into clear, practical operating procedures the team can follow each day.
•	Set quality objectives and workable plans that keep customers satisfied while making efficient use of the farm's people, water, inputs and equipment.
•	Plan and run internal audits, and coordinate external and certification audits, so the business stays inspection ready throughout the year.
•	Use quality checks, data and monitoring tools to track produce quality from the field through grading, packing and dispatch, and step in quickly when results drift outside acceptable limits.
•	Investigate non-conformances, quality issues and customer complaints, identify the root cause, and put corrective and preventive actions in place so problems do not recur.
•	Keep quality documentation, records and reporting systems accurate and current, including full batch traceability from paddock to customer.
•	Oversee hygiene, sanitation and safe food-handling practices across the packing shed, cool rooms and produce-handling areas, and keep cleaning and pest-control programmes on track.
•	Carry out pre-harvest and post-harvest inspections and product grading, confirming that fruit and vegetables meet quality specifications before they are packed and shipped.
•	Monitor storage and cool-chain conditions so freshness and shelf life are protected from harvest right through to delivery.
•	Maintain records of approved inputs and treatment activity in line with organic certification, and verify that incoming materials and supplier products meet our requirements.
•	Review how we grow, harvest, pack and dispatch, looking for practical improvements to systems, processes and workflows that lift consistency and reduce waste.
•	Train and support farm and packing staff on quality procedures, food safety and compliance, building good practice into everyday work.
•	Act as the main point of contact on quality matters for management, auditors, regulators and customers, keeping each informed on performance and compliance.
•	Champion continuous-improvement initiatives across production and operations, encouraging a culture where quality is everyone's responsibility.

About you:
•	At least 2 years of relevant experience in quality assurance, food safety or quality management, ideally gained in horticulture, fresh produce, food manufacturing or a related industry.
•	A bachelor's degree or higher qualification in food science, agricultural science, quality management or a related discipline.

Personal attributes:
•	Strong attention to detail with a methodical, organised approach to records, checks and reporting.
•	A confident communicator who can train staff and work comfortably with auditors, regulators and customers.
•	Sound problem-solving skills and a calm considered manner when quality issues arise.
•	Hands-on and approachable, at ease moving between the office, the packing shed and the field.
•	High standards of integrity and accountability, with a genuine commitment to food safety and quality.

Salary and employment conditions:
•	Permanent, full-time position of 38 hours per week.
•	$75,000 to $80,000 plus superannuation per annum.

If this sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you! Please be sure to combine a covering letter addressing the key criteria set out above as the first page of your resume.
result.title: Quality Assurance Manager

The role:
As a Software Developer and Database Administrator for City Beach, you will be responsible for designing, configuring, maintaining and supporting applications and database platforms and related data services to ensure data integrity, security, backup, reliability and performance. The role also supports internal reporting and analytics solutions by ensuring data structures, SQL queries, integrations and documentation are accurate, secure and maintainable. This is a full-time position working an average of 38 hours per week based in Brisbane, Queensland.  

Key Responsibilities:
Design, configure, maintain and support database management systems, database architecture, schemas, tables, data structures, data dictionaries and naming conventions to ensure data accuracy and completeness. 
Design, develop, test, deploy and maintain internal software applications and tools. 
Implement, administer and monitor database security, access controls, data integrity controls, backup processes, recovery procedures and disaster recovery planning. 
Perform operational and preventative maintenance for database environments, including scheduled backups, recovery testing, patching, capacity checks and routine health monitoring. 
Write, maintain and optimise SQL queries, stored procedures, views, data extracts, transformations and data models to support reporting, analytics, integrations and operational decision-making. 
Investigate, troubleshoot and resolve database issues, application data issues, performance concerns, failed jobs, data quality exceptions and other incidents affecting business systems whilst encompassing workstations and communication infrastructure.   
Test database systems and upgrades by debugging, tracking, reproducing, logging and resolving issues in accordance with approved testing scripts, procedures and quality processes. 
Prepare and maintain database documentation, including data models, data dictionaries, standards, operational procedures, security guidelines, recovery instructions and system logs. 
Monitor database, application and infrastructure performance to ensure system components operate reliably together, and recommend enhancements to improve availability, scalability, security and performance. 
Develop, maintain and enhance internal reporting solutions and dashboards, including Power BI reports and business performance dashboards, using accurate and governed data sources. 
Collaborate with stakeholders, security vendors, software suppliers and service providers to analyse user, system, database and reporting requirements and deliver practical, secure and maintainable technical solutions. 

About You:
Bachelor’s degree in relevant field or minimum 5 years experience in a similar role
Strong technical knowledge of database administration, database design, data modelling, relational database concepts and data analysis techniques. 
Sound understanding of programming languages such as C#, C++, Python. 
Strong technical knowledge of data models, database design, development, and data analysis techniques 
Proven experience maintaining database environments, including backup and recovery, data integrity controls, performance monitoring, troubleshooting and disaster recovery practices. 
Proficient in writing, maintaining and optimising SQL queries, stored procedures, views, extracts and data transformations. 
Sound understanding of database security principles, access controls, auditability, operational risk and change control processes. 
Experience developing reports, dashboards and data visualisations, including Power BI or similar tools, using accurate and governed data sources. 
Excellent analytical skills with the ability to collect, interpret, and present complex data with accuracy and attention to detail. 

Why Join Us: 
40% team member discount for you, your friends and family to access. 
Access to our Beach Benefits Program where we have partnered with industry leaders to bring our team members discounts on products and memberships to keep you healthy on all fronts. 
Access to Psych Health our Employee Assistance Program. 
Prezzee Gift Cards for major milestones and yearly anniversary celebrations. 
Weekly shared morning tea to celebrate team member milestones. 
Friday 4pm finishes and social drinks every week.? 

Annual income for standard 38 hour week is $85,000 to $95,000 plus superannuation commensurate with industry rate, skills and experience.  

City Beach appreciates the value of a diverse workforce, and we are passionate about actively seeking to accommodate the unique needs of all people. ## Position Overview
We are looking for a skilled and detail-oriented Cyber Security Advice and Assessment Specialist to join our team and play a pivotal role in safeguarding our organisation's information assets and digital infrastructure. This position is responsible for conducting security assessments, interpreting policies, and delivering expert guidance on cyber security strategies and risk management. The ideal candidate brings a strong technical foundation combined with the ability to communicate complex security concepts to a broad range of stakeholders. This role suits a proactive professional who thrives in dynamic environments and is committed to continuously strengthening an organisation's security posture.
## Key Responsibilities
- Conduct comprehensive risk assessments and security control evaluations to identify vulnerabilities and weaknesses across the organisation's systems, networks, and cyber security policies
- Perform vulnerability testing and threat analysis, translating findings into actionable recommendations that reduce exposure and strengthen overall defences
- Provide specialist advice and practical guidance on security strategies, helping stakeholders understand and effectively manage identified risks and emerging threats
- Develop, implement, and maintain security policies, standards, procedures, and guidelines that support a robust and consistent organisational security posture
- Lead and support investigations into security incidents, producing clear and thorough reports on findings and guiding the refinement of detection and response processes
- Assist with root cause analysis following security incidents or breaches, assessing the extent of impact and recommending appropriate remedial and preventative actions
- Review and assess information system designs to ensure security requirements are embedded throughout development and implementation lifecycles
- Develop and maintain meaningful metrics and reporting frameworks that articulate the impact of cyber security risks on business processes and information assets
- Align and coordinate internal and external audit activities, security assessments, and compliance engagements to ensure consistent and efficient outcomes
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to embed security best practices across business operations and technology initiatives
- Communicate complex security concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences, providing guidance that enables informed decision-making at all levels of the organisation
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- Bachelor's degree in Cyber Security, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related discipline
- Demonstrated experience in a cyber security role with a focus on risk assessment, security advisory, or security operations
- Strong working knowledge of security frameworks and standards such as ISO 27001, NIST, ASD Essential Eight, or equivalent
- Proven ability to conduct vulnerability assessments, penetration testing coordination, and security control reviews
- Experience developing and implementing security policies, standards, and procedures within a complex organisational environment
- Solid understanding of network security, cloud security principles, identity and access management, and secure system design
- Experience investigating and reporting on security incidents, including root cause analysis and post-incident remediation
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to assess risk and prioritise effectively
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to produce clear reports and present findings to diverse audiences
- Familiarity with audit coordination and compliance assessment processes across regulatory or industry frameworks
- Ability to work both autonomously and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team
## Preferred Qualifications
- Relevant industry certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, CompTIA Security+, or CEH
- Experience working within Australian Government security frameworks or with protective security requirements
- Familiarity with the Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) guidelines and the Information Security Manual (ISM)
- Postgraduate qualifications in Cyber Security, Risk Management, or a related field
- Experience with security information and event management (SIEM) platforms or other security tooling
- Prior exposure to governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platforms or tools
## Why Join Us?
- Be part of a collaborative and forward-thinking team that values innovation, continuous learning, and genuine contribution to meaningful security outcomes
- Access ongoing professional development opportunities, including support for industry certifications and training programmes
- Enjoy a flexible working environment that supports work-life balance through hybrid arrangements and adaptable scheduling
- Contribute to high-impact work that directly protects critical systems and supports the organisation's strategic objectives
- Competitive remuneration package with clear pathways for career growth and advancement within the cyber security function
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Super

Our elite sales team is made up of passionate, dedicated professionals, delivering the most advanced medical technologies to patients in need. By collaborating extensively with leading healthcare professionals you’ll see first-hand the impact you have on individual lives - one patient at a time. 

The position of Clinical Specialist, Electrophysiology (EP), provides field/remote clinical, technical & educational support in EP to assigned accounts across ANZ. Frequent travel will be required as part of the role. 

The Clinical Specialist – Electrophysiology role is based in Queensland and reports to the Field Clinical Specialist Manager.

•	Utilising your technical knowledge of:
o	The field of electrophysiology (including propagation of electrical circuits within cardiac tissue and the pathophysiology of electrical rhythm disorders), biophysics of radiofrequency, cryo-thermal ablation, 2D and 3D electroanatomical mapping principles to provide:
?	Clinical support including basic trouble-shooting, and clinical guidance to diagnose and treat cardiac arrhythmias
?	Provide the measurement of electrical circuits within the heart and perform stimulation protocols as per physician requests to measure the electrical conductivity of the heart to aid in the diagnosis of cardiac arrhythmias

Solicitor 
Gun Law Office – Knoxfield, VIC, 3180 
Permanent, full-time | $80,000 – $85,000 plus superannuation 

About us

Gun Law Office is a legal practice located in Knoxfield, Victoria, providing legal services to individuals, families and businesses.

The firm advises and represents clients across a range of practice areas, including commercial law, corporate law, business transactions, commercial and retail leasing, property law, wills and estates, trusts, family law, family violence matters, civil litigation and general legal advisory work.

The practice assists clients with both transactional and dispute-related matters, including legal advice, document preparation, negotiations, court and tribunal processes, settlements, powers of attorney, affidavits, statutory declarations and cross-border legal documentation.

Due to the evolving needs of the practice, Gun Law Office is seeking a suitably qualified Solicitor to join its team on a permanent, full-time basis.

The role 

We are seeking a qualified Solicitor to assist with the day-to-day conduct of client matters, from initial instructions through to finalisation, under the supervision and direction of the Principal and senior legal practitioners where required.

The role will involve assessing client instructions, identifying relevant legal issues, conducting legal research, preparing advice and correspondence, drafting and reviewing legal documents, managing client files, and assisting with negotiations, settlements, court processes and tribunal matters.

The successful candidate will be expected to work across both advisory and dispute-related matters, including preparing matters for conferences, mediations, hearings and other procedural events. The role also involves regular liaison with clients, counsel, courts, tribunals, government authorities, settlement agents, other legal practitioners and external stakeholders.

This position requires strong legal drafting, research, analytical and communication skills. The successful candidate must be able to manage competing deadlines, maintain accurate file records, exercise sound professional judgement and ensure all work is performed in accordance with professional, ethical and regulatory obligations.

 Key duties and responsibilities 

•	Take client instructions, identify legal issues and assist in advising clients on appropriate legal options and processes.
•	Conduct legal research and prepare advice, correspondence, file notes, case summaries and other legal documents.
•	Draft, review and settle affidavits, statutory declarations, court documents, contracts, leases, settlement documents, powers of attorney, wills and other legal instruments.
•	Assist with commercial, corporate, property, conveyancing, leasing, wills and estates, trusts, family law, family violence, civil litigation and dispute resolution matters.
•	Prepare matters for court, tribunal, mediation and conference attendances, including reviewing evidence, preparing chronologies, briefing counsel and arranging supporting documents.
•	Attend and appear before courts and tribunals where appropriate, including the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia, the Magistrates’ Court of Victoria, VCAT and other relevant courts and tribunals.
•	Assist with negotiations, settlements and dispute resolution processes in accordance with client instructions and under supervision.
•	Liaise with clients, counsel, courts, tribunals, government authorities, settlement agents, other legal practitioners and external stakeholders.
•	Manage client files under supervision from commencement to completion, including maintaining accurate file records, diarising deadlines and monitoring matter progress.
•	Prepare, review and witness powers of attorney, statutory declarations, affidavits, certifications and other Australian or overseas legal documents requiring execution, attestation or authentication.
•	Assist with cross-border legal documentation, including powers of attorney, statutory declarations, affidavits and related documents used in Sri Lankan or other overseas legal matters.
•	Ensure all work is performed in accordance with professional conduct rules, ethical obligations, confidentiality requirements, court rules, regulatory obligations and firm procedures.

Required qualifications, experience and skills 

•	Admission as an Australian legal practitioner; 
•	Current Victorian practising certificate, or eligibility to hold one; 
•	Bachelor of Laws, Juris Doctor or equivalent qualification; 
•	At least one year of relevant legal experience in private practice, in-house practice, litigation support, family law, property law, conveyancing, commercial advisory work or related legal work; 
•	Strong legal drafting, research, communication and file management skills; 
•	Ability to prepare and review legal correspondence, court documents, affidavits, contracts, leases, settlement documents, wills, powers of attorney and other legal instruments; 
•	Ability to manage competing deadlines, work under supervision and attend courts, tribunals, mediations, settlements and client conferences as required; and 
•	Professional proficiency in Sinhala will be highly regarded as many of the firm’s clients require language support to provide accurate instructions and properly understand legal advice and documents.

How to apply 

We welcome applications from all appropriately qualified candidates. Gun Law Office is committed to a fair and inclusive recruitment process and will consider applicants based on their qualifications, skills, experience and suitability for the role.

Your application should include:

•	A current resume outlining your qualifications, admission status, practising certificate status and relevant work experience; and
•	A one page cover letter addressing your suitability for the role.

To ensure all applications are properly received and assessed, please submit your application via one platform only and do not apply through multiple job portals.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
